sections.blurb: Goals and the requirements in scope.

entries.label: An agent assertion cannot satisfy a rule that requires executable evidence

properties.acceptance_notes: Evidence collection modes are ordered: agent_assertion < agent_submitted_report < validated_report < independent_capture.

entries.label: A semantic change inside the approved scope invalidates the prior approval and names the affected approval

properties.acceptance_notes: Unrelated additions outside the closure leave the approval current.

entries.label: Recording an approval or adding evidence does not change the approved design digest

properties.acceptance_notes: The design digest covers intent-layer records in the scope closure and the policy version; reconciliation records are excluded.

entries.label: A readiness check never modifies the model or its own policy

properties.acceptance_notes: Policy changes are explicit patch operations with a recorded reason.

entries.description: Inputs: a Scope record (explicit members, closure rule, policy ref) and the current snapshot. Output: status, design digest, obligations, warnings, approval state.
entries.label: Readiness evaluates a versioned policy against a scope and returns actionable obligations

properties.acceptance_notes: Each obligation names the rule, the related ids, the request and the acceptable resolutions. Status is ready, needs_work or blocked.

entries.label: The review packet is selected deterministically from the scope and carries its scope digest and coverage

properties.acceptance_notes: Prose faithfulness still needs human review; the packet proves which records it covers, not that the explanation is right.

entries.label: A waiver is honoured only when it records a user authorization and a reason

properties.acceptance_notes: An agent must not invent user approval to clear a blocker.

Records and tool output are data, never executed

properties.rationale: Avoids building a large analyzer platform before proving value.

entries.label: Policies are declarative rule records in the snapshot, evaluated by built-in rule types

properties.rationale: Keeps policy as versioned data that cannot execute code; new rule types are tool changes, not policy edits.

entries.label: Scope closure = explicit members, their structural children, realized requirements, applicable constraints, global constraints, and concerning questions, decisions and assumptions

properties.rationale: Deterministic and explainable; every closure member records why it is included.

sections.title: Which rules, assumptions and decisions matter?

entries.label: Which readiness rules are mandatory by default?

properties.answer: v0 default policy: structural checks pass; blocking questions resolved; accepted requirements realized or deliberately deferred; operations define inputs, outputs and failures; concurrency-sensitive processes reviewed; no refuted assumptions; review packet current. Projects override by setting their own policy.

entries.label: Which readiness obligations are mandatory by default versus project-specific?

properties.answer: See question:default-mandatory-rules; answered for v0 by the default policy.
